mcqs.question: The sodium–potassium pump moves, for each ATP used:
mcqs.explanation: Na+–K+ ATPase pumps 3 Na+ out and 2 K+ into the cell per ATP.

mcqs.question: The main cation of the intracellular fluid is:
mcqs.explanation: K+ is about 140 mmol/L inside cells; Na+ is the main ECF cation.

mcqs.question: In an adult man, total body water is about what percentage of body weight?
mcqs.explanation: About 60%: two-thirds intracellular and one-third extracellular.

mcqs.question: Glucose entry into most cells by a carrier, down its gradient and without ATP, is called:
mcqs.explanation: GLUT carriers move glucose down its gradient; the process shows saturation.

mcqs.question: Red cells placed in a hypotonic solution will:
mcqs.explanation: Water enters the cells by osmosis, causing swelling and haemolysis.

mcqs.question: Which is an example of positive feedback?
options: Oxytocin and uterine contractions in labour
mcqs.explanation: In labour each contraction releases more oxytocin until delivery ends the loop.

mcqs.question: DNA is replicated during which phase of the cell cycle?
mcqs.explanation: S (synthesis) phase copies DNA; G1 and G2 are growth phases.

mcqs.question: Sebaceous glands release their secretion by which mode?
mcqs.explanation: The whole sebaceous cell disintegrates to become the secretion.

mcqs.question: Plasma makes up about what fraction of the extracellular fluid?
mcqs.explanation: Plasma is about 1/4 of ECF; interstitial fluid about 3/4.

mcqs.question: Granulation tissue is characteristic of which phase of wound healing?
mcqs.explanation: Fibroblasts and new capillaries form granulation tissue in the proliferative phase.

mcqs.question: Normal tidal volume in an adult is about:
mcqs.explanation: Tidal volume is about 500 mL; 150 mL is dead space.

mcqs.question: Surfactant is secreted by:
mcqs.explanation: Type II pneumocytes secrete surfactant, which lowers surface tension.

mcqs.question: The major part of carbon dioxide is carried in blood as:
mcqs.explanation: About 70% of CO2 is carried as bicarbonate.

mcqs.question: A shift of the oxygen–haemoglobin dissociation curve to the right is caused by:
mcqs.explanation: Bohr effect: CO2, H+, heat and 2,3-BPG shift the curve right.

mcqs.question: The strongest normal stimulus to breathing is:
mcqs.explanation: CO2 forms H+ in CSF, stimulating the central chemoreceptors.

mcqs.question: Vital capacity equals:
mcqs.explanation: VC = inspiratory reserve + tidal + expiratory reserve volume (about 4600 mL).

mcqs.question: Cyanosis appears when reduced haemoglobin in capillary blood exceeds about:
mcqs.explanation: More than about 5 g/dL of deoxygenated Hb gives a bluish colour.

mcqs.question: Hypoxia due to cyanide poisoning is of which type?
mcqs.explanation: Cyanide blocks cellular use of oxygen.

mcqs.question: The pneumotaxic centre is located in the:
mcqs.explanation: The pneumotaxic centre in the upper pons limits inspiration.

mcqs.question: Normal partial pressure of oxygen in alveolar air is about:
mcqs.explanation: Alveolar PO2 is about 104 mmHg; mixed venous blood is about 40.

mcqs.question: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach is secreted by:
mcqs.explanation: Parietal (oxyntic) cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor.

mcqs.question: Intrinsic factor is required for the absorption of:
mcqs.explanation: B12 bound to intrinsic factor is absorbed in the terminal ileum.

mcqs.question: Trypsinogen is converted to trypsin by:
mcqs.explanation: Enterokinase from the duodenal mucosa activates trypsinogen.

mcqs.question: Secretin stimulates the pancreas to secrete juice rich in:
mcqs.explanation: Secretin gives watery bicarbonate-rich juice; CCK gives enzyme-rich juice.

mcqs.question: The largest share of gastric secretion occurs in which phase?
mcqs.explanation: The gastric phase gives about 60% of secretion.

mcqs.question: Products of fat digestion leave intestinal cells mainly as:
options: Free fatty acids into portal blood
mcqs.explanation: Triglycerides are re-formed and packed as chylomicrons that enter lymph.

mcqs.question: Salivary secretion is controlled by:
mcqs.explanation: Salivation is purely reflex, mainly parasympathetic.

mcqs.question: Gall bladder contraction is stimulated by:
mcqs.explanation: CCK released by fat in the duodenum contracts the gall bladder.

mcqs.question: Glucose is absorbed from the intestine mainly by:
mcqs.explanation: SGLT1 carries glucose with Na+; this is the basis of ORS.

mcqs.question: Mass movements of the colon after meals are due to the:
mcqs.explanation: Food entering the stomach triggers mass movements in the colon.

mcqs.question: The pacemaker of the heart is the:
mcqs.explanation: The SA node fires fastest (about 70–80/min) and sets the rate.

mcqs.question: The first heart sound is due to closure of:
mcqs.explanation: S1 marks AV valve closure at the start of ventricular systole.

mcqs.question: Normal cardiac output in an adult at rest is about:
mcqs.explanation: CO = 70 mL × 72 beats ≈ 5 L/min.

mcqs.question: Baroreceptors that regulate blood pressure are located in the:
mcqs.explanation: Stretch receptors in the carotid sinus and aortic arch sense pressure.

mcqs.question: Pulse pressure is:
mcqs.explanation: Pulse pressure is about 120 − 80 = 40 mmHg.

mcqs.question: The normal life span of red blood cells is about:
mcqs.explanation: RBCs live about 120 days and are removed mainly in the spleen.

mcqs.question: Erythropoietin is produced mainly by the:
mcqs.explanation: The kidneys release erythropoietin in response to hypoxia.

mcqs.question: Haemophilia A is due to deficiency of factor:
mcqs.explanation: Factor VIII lack causes haemophilia A; factor IX lack causes haemophilia B.

mcqs.question: A person with blood group AB has in the plasma:
mcqs.explanation: AB has both antigens, so no ABO antibodies — the universal recipient.

mcqs.question: The immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta is:
mcqs.explanation: IgG gives the newborn passive immunity; IgA is in breast milk.

mcqs.question: The most numerous white blood cells in normal blood are:
mcqs.explanation: Neutrophils make up about 50–70% of the differential count.

mcqs.question: Coronary blood flow to the left ventricle occurs mainly during:
mcqs.explanation: Contracting muscle compresses coronary vessels in systole.

mcqs.question: Antidiuretic hormone is synthesised in the:
mcqs.explanation: ADH is made in the hypothalamus and stored in the posterior pituitary.

mcqs.question: Deficiency of thyroid hormone in infancy causes:
mcqs.explanation: Congenital hypothyroidism (cretinism) causes mental and physical retardation.

mcqs.question: Parathyroid hormone:
mcqs.explanation: PTH increases bone resorption, renal calcium reabsorption and vitamin D activation.

mcqs.question: The only hormone that lowers blood glucose is:
mcqs.explanation: Insulin from β cells lowers blood glucose; the others raise it.

mcqs.question: Aldosterone is secreted by the:
mcqs.explanation: The outer zona glomerulosa secretes mineralocorticoids.

mcqs.question: Melatonin is secreted by the:
mcqs.explanation: Melatonin from the pineal, secreted in darkness, sets circadian rhythm.

mcqs.question: Myopia is corrected by a:
mcqs.explanation: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; a diverging lens corrects it.

mcqs.question: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of:
mcqs.explanation: Rhodopsin in rods is made from vitamin A.

mcqs.question: Taste sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by the:
mcqs.explanation: The chorda tympani branch of the facial nerve carries it.

mcqs.question: The primary auditory area is located in the:
mcqs.explanation: Areas 41 and 42 of the temporal lobe receive hearing.

mcqs.question: During skeletal muscle contraction, calcium binds to:
mcqs.explanation: Ca2+ binding to troponin C moves tropomyosin and exposes actin sites.

mcqs.question: Calcium for skeletal muscle contraction is released from the:
mcqs.explanation: The action potential in T tubules triggers Ca2+ release from the SR.

mcqs.question: Rigor mortis is due to:
mcqs.explanation: Without ATP, myosin heads cannot detach from actin.

mcqs.question: Cells that resorb bone are:
mcqs.explanation: Osteoclasts break down bone and release calcium.

mcqs.question: The shoulder joint is an example of:
mcqs.explanation: The rounded head of the humerus fits the glenoid cavity.

mcqs.question: Cardiac muscle cannot be tetanised because it has a:
mcqs.explanation: The refractory period lasts nearly as long as contraction.

mcqs.question: Intercalated discs are found in:
mcqs.explanation: They contain gap junctions that make cardiac muscle a syncytium.

mcqs.question: In smooth muscle, calcium binds to:
mcqs.explanation: Ca2+–calmodulin activates myosin light-chain kinase.

mcqs.question: The neurotransmitter at the neuromuscular junction is:
mcqs.explanation: ACh acts on nicotinic receptors of the motor end plate.

mcqs.question: The first stage of fracture healing is:
mcqs.explanation: Bleeding forms a clot between the bone ends first.

mcqs.question: Normal glomerular filtration rate is about:
mcqs.explanation: GFR is about 125 mL/min, about 180 L/day.

mcqs.question: Most of the filtered sodium and water is reabsorbed in the:
mcqs.explanation: The PCT reabsorbs about 65% of filtered Na+ and water.

mcqs.question: The renal threshold for glucose is about:
mcqs.explanation: Above about 180 mg/dL glucose spills into urine.

mcqs.question: Water reabsorption in the collecting duct is controlled by:
mcqs.explanation: ADH inserts aquaporins into collecting duct cells.

mcqs.question: The spinal centre for micturition is at:
mcqs.explanation: Pelvic parasympathetic nerves from S2–S4 contract the detrusor.

mcqs.question: Ovulation is triggered by a surge of:
mcqs.explanation: High oestrogen triggers the LH surge about day 14.

mcqs.question: The secretory phase of the endometrium is due mainly to:
mcqs.explanation: Progesterone makes the endometrium secretory for implantation.

mcqs.question: Fertilisation normally occurs in the:
mcqs.explanation: The ampulla is the usual site; the zygote then moves to the uterus.

mcqs.question: Testosterone is secreted by:
mcqs.explanation: Leydig (interstitial) cells secrete testosterone under LH.

mcqs.question: Milk ejection (let-down) is caused by:
mcqs.explanation: Suckling releases oxytocin, which contracts myoepithelial cells.

mcqs.question: The resting membrane potential of a neuron is about:
mcqs.explanation: Inside the neuron is about 70 mV negative at rest.

mcqs.question: Depolarisation during an action potential is due to:
mcqs.explanation: Voltage-gated Na+ channels open and Na+ rushes in.

mcqs.question: The vital centres for heart rate, blood pressure and respiration are located in the:
mcqs.explanation: The medulla holds the cardiac, vasomotor and respiratory centres.

mcqs.question: Intention tremor is a sign of a lesion of the:
mcqs.explanation: Cerebellar damage causes tremor on purposeful movement.

mcqs.question: A positive Babinski sign in an adult indicates a lesion of the:
mcqs.explanation: Extensor plantar response indicates corticospinal (UMN) damage.

mcqs.question: Pain and temperature are carried by the:
mcqs.explanation: The lateral spinothalamic tract crosses in the cord and carries pain and temperature.

mcqs.question: CSF is formed mainly by the:
mcqs.explanation: Choroid plexuses of the ventricles produce most CSF.

mcqs.question: The postganglionic neurotransmitter of most sympathetic fibres is:
mcqs.explanation: Most sympathetic postganglionic fibres release noradrenaline; sweat glands use ACh.

mcqs.question: Cardiac pain referred to the inner side of the left arm is explained by:
options: Convergence of afferents on the same spinal segment
Direct nerve supply of the arm by the heart
mcqs.explanation: Visceral and skin afferents share spinal neurons, so the brain misplaces the pain.

mcqs.question: Rotational movements of the head are detected by the:
mcqs.explanation: The crista ampullaris in the semicircular canals senses angular acceleration.

mcqs.question: The knee jerk reflex is mediated by spinal segments:
mcqs.explanation: The patellar reflex uses the femoral nerve, L2–L4.

mcqs.question: Total volume of CSF at any time in an adult is about:
mcqs.explanation: About 150 mL; about 500 mL is formed each day.
